lines.en: Welcome back, Ravi! Your cousin told me you spent the whole winter in Winnipeg. It must have been hard to get used to the snow.
lines.pt: Bem-vinda de volta, Ravi! Sua prima me contou que você passou o inverno inteiro em Winnipeg. Deve ter sido difícil se acostumar com a neve.

lines.en: Honestly, I had terrible culture shock at first. Minus thirty felt like another planet.
lines.pt: Sinceramente, tive um choque cultural terrível no começo. Trinta negativos pareciam outro planeta.

lines.en: I can imagine! Were you homesick? I cried to my mother every Sunday that first month.
lines.pt: Imagino! Você sentiu saudade de casa? Eu chorava com minha mãe todo domingo naquele primeiro mês.

lines.en: Constantly. I missed the beach and my friends. And in the first week I slipped on the ice three times on my way to class.
lines.pt: O tempo todo. Eu sentia falta da praia e dos meus amigos. E na primeira semana escorreguei no gelo três vezes a caminho da aula.

lines.en: Ouch! How did you cope? It takes patience, and a good pair of boots.
lines.pt: Ai! Como você lidou com isso? Exige paciência e um bom par de botas.

lines.en: Both helped. I forced myself to adapt and joined a skating club. It took a while to get used to the cold, but it got easier.
lines.pt: As duas ajudaram. Me obriguei a me adaptar e entrei num clube de patinação. Levou um tempo para me acostumar com o frio, mas ficou mais fácil.

lines.en: Good plan. Tell me about the food. Did you eat anything strange, or stick to what you knew?
lines.pt: Boa estratégia. Conte da comida. Você comeu algo estranho, ou ficou no que conhecia?

lines.en: The soup was fine, but I never got used to the coffee. It tasted like hot water with a hint of burnt toast.
lines.pt: A sopa estava boa, mas nunca me acostumei com o café. Tinha gosto de água quente com um toque de torrada queimada.

lines.en: Ha! That's cruel. I watched Nanook of the North last night, and it made me admire how people cope with the ice for months.
lines.pt: Ha! Que maldade. Assisti a Nanook of the North ontem à noite, e isso me fez admirar como as pessoas lidam com o gelo por meses.

lines.en: I love that film! I keep thinking about the scene where he builds an igloo in under an hour.
lines.pt: Adoro esse filme! Não paro de pensar na cena em que ele constrói um iglu em menos de uma hora.

lines.en: Let's watch it together this weekend, then. I'll make hot chocolate, and you can tell me what real winter feels like.
lines.pt: Então vamos assistir juntas neste fim de semana. Eu faço chocolate quente, e você me conta como é um inverno de verdade, como é.

facts.label: Get used to
facts.sub: Processo de adaptação: It took a while to get used to the cold. Passado: got used to. Presente: I’m getting used to. Depois de to, use -ing.

facts.label: Acostumar-se
facts.sub: Use get used to + -ing para o processo de se acostumar: It took a while to get used to the cold. Forma: get + used to + -ing ou substantivo. Em português: “me acostumar”.

facts.label: Processo ≠ estado
facts.sub: I’m getting used to the cold = ainda estou me acostumando. I’m used to the cold = já estou acostumado. Get used to mostra a mudança; be used to, o estado já atingido.

pages.title: Mito ou fato? · 1/2

items.s: Get used to means to become accustomed to something.
After get used to, we use the infinitive.
“I got used to the cold” is about a change in the past.

pages.instruction: Decida e explique com suas palavras.

solo: Aluno responde e justifica; você mostra a pista.
group: Cada aluno decide sozinho, depois compare as respostas e peça uma justificativa.
Corrija pela pista do texto, não só dizendo “certo/errado”.
extra90: Peça que cada aluno invente uma pergunta igual para o colega.
answers: Get used to means to become accustomed to something. → Verdadeiro (Yes.)
After get used to, we use the infinitive. → Falso (We use -ing or a noun.)
“I got used to the cold” is about a change in the past. → Verdadeiro (Yes.)

pages.title: Back home after a year in the snow · 1/3
paragraphs: It is a warm afternoon in Perth. Theo has just come home after a year in the snow. He was homesick for months. His friend Owen wants to hear everything. Living abroad was hard, and culture shock was real. They talk about how he learned to adapt.

“Welcome back, Theo! It must have been hard to get used to the snow after growing up in Perth.” says Owen. “It took a while to get used to the cold. At first I couldn’t get used to wearing three jackets.” says Theo. “How long did it take you to get used to the dark afternoons? Winter there starts so early.” says Owen.

pages.title: Back home after a year in the snow · 3/3
paragraphs: “Some people never get used to it. It takes patience, and you have to stop comparing everything with home.” says Theo. “Wise words. I’ll try to get used to the cold mornings here before next winter, then!” says Owen. Theo laughs and orders another coffee. He misses the snow, but not the dark days. Owen asks to see the photos. They sit in the sun and talk. Patience helped him cope with everything. Now Theo is getting used to the heat again.
